requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and the real service already agree: the page heading stands as the question, and screen-reader users hear the legend as the group's name.

requirements.statement: In the live-animals set the main import reason is one radio choice of five reasons, in this order: Internal market; Transhipment or onward travel; Transit; Re-entry; Temporary admission horses. No reason is pre-selected on a notification without one, and the list is the same for every live-animal commodity (cattle, horses). The live page never reduces the list: no live-animals notification holds germinal products, and the germinal set's own copy of the page carries its two-reason list (req-169).
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and the real service offer the same five reasons in the same order; the 9 October ruling puts germinal products in a sibling set with its own catalogue, so the germinal reduction belongs to that set's copy, not the live page.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p7-007 and trace-animals-fit-p7-013 show the five reasons in this order today.

requirements.statement: Each reason carries its hint: Internal market 'For imports of animals intended for sale or use in Great Britain (England, Scotland or Wales).'; Transhipment or onward travel 'For animals intended for direct travel to a third country, that will stay only within the same port or airport in Great Britain while moving to another means of transport.'; Transit 'For animals moving through Great Britain for direct travel to a third country, that will enter Great Britain at one port or airport and leave from a different one within England, Scotland or Wales.'; Re-entry 'For animals authorised for re-entry, or rejected exports re-entering Great Britain.'; Temporary admission horses 'For horses authorised for temporary entry.'
requirements.why: The five hints are word for word the same in Design Release 2.1 and the real service.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p7-008 to repo-frontend-p7-012 hold the same five hints today.

requirements.statement: A main import reason is optional to proceed: Save and continue with no reason chosen shows no error and moves on.

requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p7-013 and trace-e2e-p5-062-m1 show a blank reason accepted today; no fit or tests-repo page test pins it (repo-tests-p1-074, trace-animals-fit-p7-076).

requirements.statement: Each reason that needs follow-up questions opens them in a standard GOV.UK conditional reveal directly under its own radio, so the reason and its follow-ups are answered in one submit; Re-entry has no reveal and saves on its own; every reveal is hidden until its reason is chosen. Without JavaScript every reveal shows open and the page still works, because only the chosen reason's follow-ups are validated and saved (req-156).
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 asks the follow-ups as reveals on the reason page; the real service moved them there in DR1 parity (inc-067), so it already matches. The 9 October afternoon ruling requires every page to work fully without JavaScript, which GOV.UK's conditional reveal already gives.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p7-015 and trace-animals-fit-p7-019 show the four reveals under their radios today, and trace-e2e-p4-104 shows Re-entry saving alone.

requirements.statement: The transhipment and transit 'Destination country' selects offer reference-data's GBNAG_SPS_EX countries plus their subdivisions, each subdivision labelled '<territory> (<parent>)', all sorted alphabetically as the origin page sorts them. requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 offers EU outermost regions and territories beside the countries, labelled with their parent. The 9 October ruling lifts DR1's MDM block, because no reference list waits on MDM: the list is built now against reference-data as it is. It also rules that list content is MDM's to own, not the prototype's.

requirements.statement: The exit date is one text field using the MOJ date picker, labelled 'Exit date' with the hint 'For example, 27/3/2026' and a 'Choose date' calendar (Monday-first weeks, picking a day fills it as day/month/year without leading zeros); a typed date in d/m/yyyy form is accepted, surrounding spaces are trimmed, and no earliest or latest date is set.

The MoJ date picker is one of the components the 9 October afternoon ruling accepts, and its design question 12 covers only the germinal dates read from a document, so the exit date keeps its calendar.

requirements.statement: Only the chosen reason's follow-ups are validated and saved; changing the reason removes the earlier reason's answers that the new one does not ask, so returning to Internal market after switching away offers no purpose and asks for it again.

requirements.statement: The notification holds one destination country and one port of exit answer, each reached through its own form field per reveal, and every reveal that asks for it is prefilled from the saved answer, so a Transit country is still offered under Transhipment.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 names a separate field per reveal, but DR1 judged that the per-branch names are a DOM artefact, not extra questions, and that carrying a shared answer between reveals is not a requirement (inc-067); that judgement on the same difference stands.

requirements.statement: The reason, internal market purpose, certification purpose and unweaned answers are stored as the service's codes (for example internalMarket, breeding, further-keeping, yes), not as their displayed labels.
requirements.why: Stored values are a persistence contract with the backend and other services that the prototype, which stores labels, cannot express; the ruling lets that constraint override the prototype.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p7-007 and trace-animals-fit-p12-007 show the coded values stored today.

requirements.statement: A submitted reason, certification purpose or unweaned value that is not one of the offered options is refused with 'Select a valid option', linking to and focusing the group's first radio, with no option left checked and the other question's valid answer kept; a refused submit writes nothing to the notification.
requirements.why: Server-side validation that refuses tampered values and never saves a refused submit is a real constraint the prototype cannot express (it silently drops or stores them), so it overrides the prototype.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p7-014, repo-frontend-p7-091 and trace-e2e-p4-115-m1 show the refusal and that nothing is written today.

requirements.statement: When either page is refused on submit, the browser title is prefixed 'Error: ' and the page is answered with HTTP 400; each inline message carries a visually hidden 'Error:' prefix.
requirements.why: The 'Error: ' title prefix is how GOV.UK tells screen-reader users a validation error has happened; the prototype's title omits it, but accessible validation is a real constraint the prototype does not express.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-animals-fit-p7-059 and trace-animals-fit-p12-029 show the 'Error: ' prefix and HTTP 400 today.

requirements.statement: When a saved destination country, port of exit or certification purpose is no longer in the reference list, reopening the page says so ('The saved destination country is no longer available. Select a country from the list.', 'The saved port of exit is no longer available. Select a port from the list.', 'The certification purpose you chose is no longer offered. Select a purpose from the list.') and blanks it in every reveal.
requirements.why: A saved answer going stale against reference data is a persistence constraint the prototype cannot express, so the real service keeps handling it.

requirements.statement: When the main import reason page is opened while editing a template from its review, the Back link goes to that template's review, and saving saves the template and returns to its review with a '<title> has been updated' message. The templates area owns the template itself.

requirements.statement: Both pages have no serious or critical WCAG 2 A or AA axe violations, including with each reveal open, in error and with the date picker open, discounting govuk-frontend's aria-expanded false positive on conditional-reveal radios.
requirements.why: Accessibility is a constraint the prototype does not express; the real service already proves it.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-animals-fit-p7-071, trace-animals-fit-p7-072 and trace-animals-fit-p12-037 show the axe results today.

requirements.statement: Both forms post to their own URL with browser validation off and carry a CSRF crumb and a concurrency token.
requirements.why: The prototype posts with novalidate too; the crumb and concurrency token are security and persistence constraints the prototype cannot express.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p7-058 and trace-animals-fit-p7-058-m2 show the hidden fields and novalidate today.

requirements.statement: Both pages keep their Welsh copy, and every English string this area changes gets its Welsh counterpart changed with it; the Welsh stays marked as a machine draft until a translator reviews it.
requirements.why: Welsh-language provision is a legal constraint the prototype does not express, so it is kept rather than removed for lack of a Design Release 2.1 counterpart.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p7-059, repo-frontend-p7-060 and repo-frontend-p7-104 show the machine-draft Welsh copy today.

requirements.statement: Both pages are built from govuk-frontend components (radios with conditional reveals, fieldset, select, hint, error summary and messages, button, back link) plus the MOJ date picker, with standard GOV.UK caption and heading classes.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 uses the same components; its custom caption and heading classes have standard GOV.UK equivalents the real service already uses. The 9 October afternoon ruling makes GOV.UK Frontend, then the accepted MoJ components, the only toolbox, with no custom JavaScript copied from the prototype.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-animals-fit-p7-074 and trace-animals-fit-p12-062 show the components today.

requirements.statement: The prototype's seed route /prototype/reason-for-import, which fills earlier answers and jumps to the reason page, is not built.
requirements.why: It is prototype tooling, not a step of the service.

requirements.statement: Prototype artefacts are not copied: its disabled page guards, its fixed fallback notification reference, forms that drop from=review, errors that linger after a soft save, a doubled error class on the date group and an unused unfiltered purpose helper.
requirements.why: These are shortcuts or defects in the prototype's session-based build, not design intent; the real service's entry guards, notification references and per-request error rendering stay as they are.

requirements.statement: No check is made between the main import reason and the certification purpose.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 asks for none, so there is nothing to build.

requirements.statement: DR1's open test-contract actions on the reveal move are not taken up here: no-JavaScript coverage of the reveals, Lighthouse audits of reveal states, and pinning the run's skip of a gated step, nor the record of its failed build attempts.
requirements.why: The ruling makes the DR1 backlog a source of judgements only, never of requirements, and Design Release 2.1 says nothing on these; they go to the report as open team decisions.

requirements.statement: The tests repo's test data holds certification purpose values the page does not offer (approvedBodies, breedingAndOrProduction).
requirements.why: It is not a Design Release 2.1 difference; it goes to the report as a tests-repo data problem.

requirements.statement: The destination country list is not edited in code to Design Release 2.1's own 41 entries, such as its Crown Dependencies shown with '(United Kingdom)' or its 'Republic of Ireland'. Where reference-data's GBNAG_SPS_EX countries and subdivisions differ from them, the difference goes to the list's owner as an MDM content question.
requirements.why: The 9 October ruling makes list content MDM's: a difference from Design Release 2.1 is never a reason to block a row or edit a list in code. DR1's deferral to the MDM integration no longer holds back the change, and gives no date for it.

requirements.statement: No exit-only list of animal-approved border control posts is built for the port of exit: neither Design Release 2.1's ten posts (for example 'Holyhead POE - GBHLY') nor a new reference-data endpoint. Nor is the hint 'Exit and entry share the same port list.' that DR1 expected while its block stood.
requirements.why: The 9 October ruling: MDM carries no approved-for-animals flag, so the whole ports-of-entry list is shown for now. If MDM adds the flag, the list can be refined later, outside this programme (deferred.md).

requirements.statement: Each 'Port of exit' option, on both the transit and the temporary admission selects, reads '<port name> - <port code>' (for example 'Port of Dover - GB DVR'), the same label the port of entry options take (req-295). The option still submits the port code.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 shows each exit port as its name then its code, after a hyphen. The prototype wins by default on how an option reads, and no DR1 judgement or real constraint covers the label. The stored value stays the code.
requirements.deltaNote: Today each option reads 'Name (CODE)' (repo-frontend-p7-037, trace-animals-fit-p7-045).

requirements.statement: The 'Port of exit' selects list the ports in the same order as the ports-of-entry list: airports first, then seaports, then rail ports in their own group. Within each group, ports are sorted A to Z by name, ignoring letter case, with non-breaking and doubled spaces normalised before comparing.
requirements.why: The 9 October ruling has the port of exit offer the whole ports-of-entry list, and orders that list by MDM's traffic value (airport, seaport, rail). The exit selects show it in that order rather than a separate one.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the ports are listed in one alphabetical run by name, airports, seaports and rail mixed (trace-animals-fit-p7-046). The traffic value reaches /ports-of-entry under req-304's row, which this follows.

requirements.statement: In the live-animals set the Additional details page applies to every notification. It always asks the certified-for question, because no live-animals notification is germinal-only, and nothing is set automatically. The unweaned question still follows req-175. The germinal-products set leaves the page out and sets certified-for itself (req-181, req-182).
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 hides the certification question, and so the page, only for germinal-only consignments. The 9 October ruling puts those in their own set and takes germinal lines out of the live catalogue. This is the live half of req-182, split per set as the ruling requires.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p7-095 and trace-animals-fit-p12-009 show the certified-for question asked for every live consignment today. The germinal lines in today's live catalogue come out under the commodity area (ruling claim 26).

requirements.statement: The main import reason page stays at the slug import-reason and Additional details at additional-details. Their form fields stay reasonForImport, purposeInInternalMarket, animalsCertifiedFor and containsUnweanedAnimals, and every radio keeps a label tied to its input by id.
requirements.why: URL paths and form field names are the real service's architecture, which the prototype never decides. The performance-test suite also drives these pages by these slugs, field names and labels.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p7-001, repo-frontend-p7-082 and repo-perftests-p1-029 to repo-perftests-p1-032 show these slugs and field names today.

requirements.statement: The main import reason and additional details rows change only the animals frontend: the high-risk plants frontend has no main import reason, certified-for or unweaned question, so it takes no change from this area.
requirements.why: The 9 October afternoon ruling changes plants in the same increment only where plants has the same page or behaviour, and never mirrors animals-only data such as ITAHC, transit or species into plants. The shared save behaviour these pages use reaches plants through its own shared rows, not this area's.

conflicts.about: Whether answers are stored as their displayed labels (prototype) or as service codes (real service).

positions.says: A real constraint the prototype cannot express, such as persistence, overrides the prototype.
Reasons, purposes and certification purposes are stored as codes such as internalMarket and further-keeping.
Each certification option submits a kebab-case code.
Each import reason's stored value is its displayed label.
Certification purposes are stored as their labels.
The prototype never decides data-model shape or form field names.

conflicts.outcome: Stored values are a persistence contract the prototype cannot express, and the 9 October ruling leaves data shape to the real service, so the service's codes stay. prototype-dr2-1-source-p4-028 is not overruled: its hints and pre-selection still stand.

conflicts.about: What happens to off-list values and to answers on a submit that fails validation.

positions.says: A real validation or persistence constraint overrides the prototype.
An off-list reason is refused with 'Select a valid option' and not kept.
A refused reason save writes nothing to the notification.
The reason and its follow-ups are saved even when the follow-ups fail validation.
Additional details saves a submitted value as given, unchecked against the options.

conflicts.outcome: Server-side validation and never persisting a refused submit are real constraints the prototype cannot express, so the real service keeps refusing off-list values with 'Select a valid option' and writes nothing on a refused submit.

conflicts.about: Whether each reveal keeps its own destination country and port of exit answer, or the notification holds one of each shared across reveals.

positions.says: inc-067: the per-branch field names are a DOM artefact; the frontend holds one destination country and one port of exit.
inc-067: a Transit country still in scope under Transhipment is an artefact, not a requirement.
Follow-up answers belonging to other reasons are cleared, so each branch starts empty.
Transhipment and transit save to one destinationCountry, transit and temporary admission to one portOfExit.
The prototype never decides form field names or data-model shape.

conflicts.outcome: DR1 already judged this same difference (inc-067), and the 9 October ruling leaves field names and data shape to the real service: the notification keeps one shared answer each, prefilled in every reveal.

conflicts.about: Whether the destination country list changes now, and whose content it takes: Design Release 2.1's entries, DR1's MDM block, or reference-data's as it is.

positions.says: req-147 is built now: the destination select offers reference-data's GBNAG_SPS_EX countries plus their subdivisions.
A list's content differing from Design Release 2.1 is MDM's to change, never a reason to block a row or edit a list in code.
List content of countries, regions and territories is master reference data deferred to the MDM integration.
inc-081: the country list holds only sovereign states where DR1 adds regions and territories; it is blocked.
The destination list is the EU states, outermost territories and Crown Dependencies.
Today the destination list is the 27 EU states plus Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway and Switzerland.

conflicts.outcome: The 9 October ruling ranks first. It lifts DR1's MDM block, though Rhys's judgement still stands for who owns list content. The destination select is built now: reference-data's GBNAG_SPS_EX countries plus their subdivisions, labelled '<territory> (<parent>)' and sorted alphabetically. Design Release 2.1's own 41 entries are not typed into code. DR1's deferral and block, and the prototype's list content, are overruled. The prototype's label shape and alphabetical order survive through the ruling's own claims.

conflicts.about: What the port of exit offers: Design Release 2.1's ten animal-approved exit border control posts, DR1's block pending MDM, or the whole ports-of-entry list.

positions.says: req-149's animal-approved exit list is replaced and c-027's block lifted: the whole list is shown for now.
No exit-only port list is built, because MDM has no approved-for-animals flag.
inc-071 is blocked: the exit list needs an approved-for-animals attribute that travels with MDM.
While blocked, exit keeps the port of entry list and its 'Exit and entry share the same port list.' hint.
The port of exit list is ten animal exit border control posts.
Today the port of exit offers every port of entry as 'Name (CODE)', with no hint.

conflicts.outcome: The 9 October ruling ranks first: both port of exit selects offer the whole ports-of-entry list now, unblocked, and no exit-only list is built. The prototype's ten posts and DR1's block are overruled. document-dr1-parity-backlog-p4-039 is not overruled, because its shared list is what is now built. Its hint is already gone today (repo-frontend-p7-036) and is not brought back.

conflicts.about: Whether the browser title is prefixed 'Error: ' when a page shows errors.

positions.says: A real validation constraint the prototype cannot express overrides it.
On a failed validation the title is prefixed 'Error: '.
With errors the title stays 'Main import reason - Import notification service - GOV.UK' with no prefix.

conflicts.outcome: The 'Error: ' prefix is GOV.UK's accessible signal of a validation error, a constraint the prototype's layout does not express, so the real service keeps it.

conflicts.about: The reason page's heading and title: 'Main import reason' or 'Main reason for import'.

positions.says: The heading and title are 'Main import reason'.
The heading and title are 'Main reason for import'.

conflicts.outcome: The prototype wins by default and no DR1 judgement or real constraint covers the heading: the page becomes 'Main import reason'. The frontend claim stays cited as the evidence of what changes.

conflicts.about: Where the reason page's Back link goes.

positions.says: Back goes to What are you importing, or to the hub when opened from it.
Back always goes to the notification hub.

conflicts.outcome: The prototype wins by default: Back goes to the previous page, or the hub when opened from it.

conflicts.about: Where Save and continue on the reason page goes next.

positions.says: It goes to Commodity details.
The opening run goes to Additional details.

conflicts.outcome: The prototype wins by default: Save and continue goes to Commodity details in the linear journey.

positions.says: It starts on 'Select one' with no divider.
It starts on 'Select a country' and a disabled divider.

conflicts.outcome: The prototype wins by default: 'Select one', no divider.

conflicts.about: The port of exit select's placeholder.

positions.says: It starts on 'Select one' with no divider.
It starts on 'Select port of exit' and a disabled divider.

conflicts.outcome: The prototype wins by default: 'Select one', no divider.

positions.says: 'You can find this information on the ITAHC.'
'This information can be found on the ITAHC.'

conflicts.outcome: The prototype wins by default: the hint becomes 'You can find this information on the ITAHC.'

conflicts.about: Which commodities are asked the unweaned question.

positions.says: Any commodity with unweaned options: cattle and pig.
Only cattle ('Cow').

conflicts.outcome: The prototype wins by default: cattle and pig are asked.

conflicts.about: Where the additional details page's Back link goes.

positions.says: Back goes to Identification details when identifiers are needed, otherwise Commodity details.
Back always goes to the notification hub.

conflicts.outcome: The prototype wins by default: Back goes to the previous journey page.

conflicts.about: Where the additional details page sits in the journey and where Save and continue goes.

positions.says: It follows identification or commodity details and Save and continue goes to Arrival details.
It follows the reason page and Save and continue returns to the overview.

conflicts.outcome: The prototype wins by default: Additional details sits after identification or commodity details and continues to Arrival details.

conflicts.about: Whether the main reason task completes on the reason's own answers or only once Additional details is saved too.

positions.says: The reason section is complete once an allowed reason and valid follow-ups are saved.
The row completes only once the Additional details page after it is saved too.

conflicts.outcome: The prototype wins by default: the reason task completes on its own answers, and Additional details is its own task.

conflicts.about: How each port of exit option reads: '<name> - <code>' or 'Name (CODE)'.

positions.says: Port of exit options are shown as the port name then its code, for example 'Edinburgh Airport (animals) - GBEDI4'.
Each port of exit option is labelled 'Name (CODE)'.

conflicts.outcome: The prototype wins by default on how an option reads, and no DR1 judgement or real constraint covers it: each option reads '<port name> - <port code>', matching the port of entry options (req-295), while the submitted value stays the code. trace-animals-fit-p7-045 is not overruled; it still shows the whole list that req-149 keeps.
